To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

LIO signals in SWIR channels are suitable for accurate trace species retrievals from occultations in the upper tropopause/lower stratospheric region, and that this can be done under all atmospheric conditions, except for clouds, where the retrieval can be limited to thin cirrus clouds.

LIO signals are suitable for accurate trace species retrievals, provided that the differential transmission principle is applied with a close signal spacing and a close time spacing of background and laser signals, and provided that a simultaneously retrieved or moderately accurate background wind profile is applied in the trace species retrievals.
LEO-LEOs can be used to accurately retrieve thermodynamic and trace species profiles in the upper tropo-/lower stratosphere outside clouds, and to retrieve cloud layering and wind profiles.
